0.long_answer: Coenzyme Q10, a naturally occurring quinone antioxidant that is part of the mitochondrial electron transport chain, helps in electron transport from NADH and succinate dehydrogenases to the cytochrome system. It is either naturally produced in the human body or obtained from dietary sources such as fish. Its ability to mitigate oxidative stress makes it useful for treating heart failure, particularly in cases of dilated cardiomyopathy, where mitochondrial dysfunction plays a significant role in disease progression.
